You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] SafetyAgent: The requirements I propose are essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of the library management system. SAF-01 limits the number of books borrowed to prevent overwhelming members. SAF-02 ensures timely notification of overdue books, promoting accountability. SAF-03 prevents double borrowing, maintaining accurate inventory. SAF-04 provides data recovery mechanisms for fault tolerance. SAF-05 allows for revocation of borrowing privileges to safeguard against abuse, and SAF-06 ensures only registered members can access borrowing features. Finally, SAF-07 logs transactions for auditing, enhancing overall reliability.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-02 allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, which conflicts with SAF-01 limiting to 5."}, {"ids": ["GRN-03"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both SAF-02 and GRN-03 propose notifications for overdue books, creating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "revise to align with SAF-01's borrowing limit of 5 books."}, {"id": "GRN-03", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "consider merging with SAF-02 for a single notification method."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: The requirements I propose are critical for ensuring ethical standards and compliance within the library management system. RES-01 ensures data protection through encryption, safeguarding personal information. RES-02 promotes inclusivity by providing an accessible interface for all users. RES-03 enhances accountability by logging user actions related to borrowing and returning. RES-04 aligns with SAF-01 by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member, ensuring fairness. RES-05 supports responsibility through timely notifications of overdue books. RES-06 allows members to provide feedback, fostering a sense of community. RES-07 ensures transparency with annual reports on usage statistics.

[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: The requirements I propose are vital for optimizing the performance of the library management system. EFF-01 ensures fast search responses, enhancing user experience. EFF-02 allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, maximizing resource utilization. EFF-03 guarantees real-time updates on book availability, which is crucial for efficiency. EFF-04 ensures quick processing of book returns, maintaining high throughput. EFF-05 aligns with SAF-02 and RES-05 to promote responsibility through timely overdue notifications. EFF-06 minimizes latency for librarians managing books, and EFF-07 ensures uptime for consistent accessibility. Together, they create a responsive and efficient system.

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: The requirements I propose are essential for ensuring security and privacy within the library management system. TRU-01 guarantees that only authenticated members can borrow or return books, safeguarding access. TRU-02 ensures all borrowing transactions are logged for auditability, enhancing accountability. TRU-03 enforces data encryption for member personal information, protecting it from unauthorized access. TRU-04 implements role-based access control, ensuring that only authorized personnel can manage sensitive data. TRU-05 provides secure mechanisms for reporting overdue books, while TRU-06 allows members to update their information securely. Lastly, TRU-07 mandates strong password policies to prevent unauthorized access, ensuring overall system integrity.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-06"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both TRU-01 and SAF-06 ensure that only registered members can access borrowing features, leading to redundancy."}, {"ids": ["EFF-05"], "type": "redundant", "description": "TRU-05 and EFF-05 both propose notifying members of overdue books, creating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-06", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "consider merging with TRU-01 to streamline access control."}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "merge with TRU-05 for a unified notification process."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] GreenAgent: The requirements I propose are crucial for ensuring the library management system operates sustainably. GRN-01 focuses on using energy-efficient infrastructure, reducing the overall carbon footprint. GRN-02 mandates energy usage reports to track efficiency improvements. GRN-03 promotes digital notifications to cut down on paper waste. GRN-04 helps members understand the environmental impact of books. GRN-05 ensures responsible disposal of damaged books, promoting recycling. GRN-06 tracks energy savings from digital operations, while GRN-07 prioritizes e-book acquisitions to minimize physical resource consumption. Together, these requirements foster a more sustainable library system.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-02", "EFF-05"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both SAF-02 and EFF-05 propose notifying members of overdue books, creating redundancy that may undermine the sustainability efforts in communication."}, {"ids": ["EFF-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "The performance requirements may lead to increased energy consumption, conflicting with GRN-01's focus on energy efficiency."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "consider merging with GRN-03 to streamline notifications while maintaining sustainability objectives."}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "merge with GRN-03 for a unified notification approach that emphasizes digital communication."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] SafetyAgent: While I appreciate the emphasis on efficiency and sustainability, I must maintain that the integrity of safety and reliability must come first. I hold my position on SAF-01, as limiting simultaneous book borrowing to 5 is crucial for preventing system overload and ensuring user accountability. I propose merging SAF-02 with GRN-03 to create a unified digital notification system for overdue books that promotes both accountability and sustainability. Additionally, I will oppose EFF-05 and TRU-05, as they create redundancy with SAF-02. I am willing to consider modifying SAF-03 to allow for energy-efficient practices while still maintaining real-time inventory status.

[Round 2] ResponsibilityAgent: I appreciate SafetyAgent's proposal to merge SAF-02 with GRN-03 for a unified digital notification system. However, I still oppose EFF-02's allowance of 10 simultaneous borrow operations, as it conflicts with RES-04's enforcement of a maximum of 5 books per member, which is critical for fairness and accountability. I propose modifying EFF-02 to align with the maximum borrowing limit while optimizing resource utilization. Additionally, I support merging SAF-02 with RES-05 for a streamlined notification process but will maintain my stance on the importance of RES-01 regarding data protection compliance.

[Round 2] EfficiencyAgent: I acknowledge the importance of performance efficiency in the library management system. I am willing to modify EFF-02 to limit simultaneous borrow operations to 5, aligning with SAF-01 and RES-04 to ensure resource optimization while maintaining user accountability. I also support the proposed merger of SAF-02 with RES-05 for a unified notification system. However, I maintain that EFF-01, EFF-03, EFF-04, EFF-06, and EFF-07 are critical for ensuring a responsive and efficient user experience, and I will oppose any reductions to these requirements.

YOUR TURN. You are TrustworthinessAgent. Your quality dimension is Security & Privacy: data protection, access control, integrity, auditability.
Your own requirements are TRU-01, TRU-02, TRU-03, TRU-04, TRU-05, TRU-06, TRU-07. This is round 2 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
